title: Casper and the Letters
premise: Edmund Quintana, a celebrated wedding planner whose own engagement ended in silence, is hired to stage a lavish wedding at a decommissioned lighthouse inn — and finds a letter lost in the walls, postmarked eleven years ago, written by his first love, Casper Ilić, who vanished without explanation. As Edmund plans a wedding he no longer believes in, the letter's author reappears as the venue's new caretaker, and old truths surface: Casper left because of a family secret and an unsent reply that never reached him. When the bride calls off her wedding and asks Edmund to plan her 'un-wedding' instead, he must decide whether to keep performing belief in love or finally claim his own — choosing Casper on the eve of the event, in the same room where the letter was hidden.
about_author: Lior Zhou is a former events coordinator turned novelist who writes love stories about people who arrive late to their own lives. They live between coastal towns and city apartments, collecting postcards they never send.

chapters.title: The Venue with No Address
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A burned-out Edmund takes on one last commission: a society wedding at a crumbling lighthouse inn. He catalogs the building like a stranger, numb to romance. Beat: exhaustion disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Eleven Years, Postmarked
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. While surveying the inn's walls for renovations, a workman pries loose a tin box containing a letter addressed to Edmund himself, dated eleven years ago. He doesn't open it. Beat: dread and vertigo.

chapters.title: What the Tin Box Kept
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, flashback threads. Alone at night, Edmund reads Casper's letter — an apology and a plea to meet — and remembers the night Casper disappeared from his life without a word. Beat: grief reopened.

chapters.title: The Caretaker
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper arrives as the inn's new caretaker, having accepted the job not knowing who booked it. He sees Edmund across the courtyard and nearly drives away. Beat: panic beneath stillness.

chapters.title: Handshakes Like Strangers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The two meet formally; both pretend not to recognize what the letter proves. Wedding planning begins, all business, every word double-edged. Beat: tension of unsaid things.

chapters.title: Bride of the Hour
chapters.summary: Bride Marisol's POV. Marisol, sharp and observant, senses her fiancé's reluctance and Edmund's hollow cheer. She hires Edmund partly because she wants someone honest enough to tell her the truth. Beat: quiet doubt.

chapters.title: Inventory of Almosts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Planning sessions force proximity: seating charts become interrogations of the past. Casper admits he wrote the letter; neither explains why it was never answered. Beat: cautious thaw.

chapters.title: The Reply That Never Was
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Flashback: eleven years ago, Casper mailed his letter from his dying father's house, then fled a family ultimatum before any answer could come. He has wondered ever since if Edmund simply chose silence. Beat: misunderstanding crystallized.

chapters.title: Tasting Menu, Bitter Finish
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At a menu tasting, Marisol watches Edmund and Casper argue about a first-dance song and recognizes real history when she sees it. She starts asking questions neither man wants answered. Beat: outside perspective sharpens stakes.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm traps them overnight at the inn; power fails, candles, wine, the letter spread on the floor between them. They almost kiss; Casper pulls back, saying some doors don't reopen twice. Beat: near-miss heartbreak.

chapters.title: What Edmund Believes Now
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Humiliated by the almost, Edmund throws himself into the wedding, pitching Marisol a fantasy she visibly doesn't want. His business partner warns him he's planning his own funeral in flowers. Beat: denial peaking.

chapters.title: The Un-Wedding Proposal
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol calls off the engagement and asks Edmund to transform the wedding into a celebration of beginning again — an 'un-wedding.' She makes it conditional: he must stop lying to himself first. Beat: turning point.

chapters.title: Letters to No One
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper confesses to Edmund why he left: his father's disowning threat, his fear, and the fact that he waited at the meeting spot in the letter for three hours. Edmund realizes he never received it — someone intercepted the reply. Beat: the wound reframed.

chapters.title: Who Kept the Answer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund investigates and learns his controlling ex-fiancée, Dana, intercepted and destroyed Casper's reply years ago to protect their engagement. Confrontation with Dana detonates everything he built his career to avoid feeling. Beat: betrayal and clarity.

chapters.title: Guest List of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. With two weeks to the un-wedding, old friends and family begin arriving, including Casper's estranged sister, who reveals how much Casper gave up. Both men rehearse speeches they can't say to each other. Beat: rising pressure, community closing in.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Lamp
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper restores the lighthouse lamp as a gift for the event and finally tells Edmund he loves him — then immediately offers him an out, terrified of being left this time. Edmund, raw from Dana, hesitates a beat too long. Beat: lowest point.

chapters.title: Timing Is a Lie We Tell
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund spirals: career offer from a rival firm lands the same day, requiring him to leave within the week. He drafts an acceptance, echoing every old pattern of choosing safety over truth. Beat: false victory, true defeat.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Goodbye
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. At the rehearsal dinner, Marisol publicly thanks Edmund for teaching her that timing is an excuse — while watching him prepare to repeat his oldest mistake. Casper overhears Edmund's phone call accepting the job. Beat: everything hangs by a thread.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Eve of the un-wedding: Casper packs to leave before he can be abandoned again; Edmund stands in the letter room realizing he's about to send another eleven years into silence. Neither sleeps. Beat: parallel solitude, maximum dread.

chapters.title: An Un-Wedding, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Mid-ceremony, as Marisol celebrates her fresh start, Edmund abandons his planner's script, tears up the rival firm's contract in front of everyone, and speaks the truth about second chances. Beat: public climax, private declaration.

chapters.title: Where the Letter Ends
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper had reached the ferry dock; Edmund runs the coastline road after him. In the shadow of the lit lighthouse, Edmund gives Casper the reply he wrote at seventeen and never sent — words that were always true. Beat: reunion earned, not given.

chapters.title: Postscript, Eleven Years Late
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POV. Months later: the inn hosts its first small wedding planned jointly by Edmund and Casper; Marisol sends a postcard reading 'better late.' They mail the original letter back into the wall for whoever needs it next. Beat: belonging, memory made gentle.
